## Details

<a id="ia.https"></a>

### 5.1 HTTPS

- Stable ID: `ia.https`
- Stage: Read
- Strength: MUST
- AR practices: none (mapping: none)
- Evidence type: `recommendation`
- Fix: Serve the site over HTTPS with a valid certificate and redirect HTTP to HTTPS.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.https)
- Evidence source: [Let's Encrypt](https://letsencrypt.org/)
- Applicability: always (website)
- Expected result: A response without a TLS error
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.https`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.https

Why: HTTPS is the baseline for secure communication. AI agents and crawlers refuse to interact with insecure sites, and browsers mark HTTP sites as unsafe.

References:

- [Let's Encrypt](https://letsencrypt.org/) (guide)
- [Why HTTPS Matters](https://web.dev/articles/why-https-matters) (guide)

Steps:

1. Install a valid TLS certificate, for example from Let's Encrypt.
2. Redirect all HTTP requests to HTTPS with a 301.

   ```nginx
   server {
     listen 80;
     return 301 https://$host$request_uri;
   }
   ```

Verify:

```bash
curl -sI https://{domain}/
```

<a id="ia.hsts"></a>

### 5.3 HSTS

- Stable ID: `ia.hsts`
- Stage: Read
- Strength: MUST
- AR practices: none (mapping: none)
- Evidence type: `recommendation`
- Fix: Send Strict-Transport-Security with a max-age of at least one year.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.hsts)
- Evidence source: [MDN: Strict-Transport-Security](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Strict-Transport-Security)
- Applicability: always (website)
- Expected result: A Strict-Transport-Security header with max-age=31536000 or higher
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.hsts`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.hsts

Why: HSTS prevents protocol downgrade attacks by telling browsers to always use HTTPS. AI agents that follow redirects benefit from HSTS as it eliminates insecure initial connections.

References:

- [MDN: Strict-Transport-Security](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Strict-Transport-Security) (guide)
- [HSTS Preload List](https://hstspreload.org/) (guide)

Steps:

1. Add the Strict-Transport-Security header to all HTTPS responses.

   ```nginx
   add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains" always;
   ```

Verify:

```bash
curl -sI https://{domain}/
```

<a id="ia.csp"></a>

### 5.4 Content-Security-Policy

- Stable ID: `ia.csp`
- Stage: Read
- Strength: MUST
- AR practices: none (mapping: none)
- Evidence type: `recommendation`
- Fix: Send a Content-Security-Policy header with default-src and script-src.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.csp)
- Evidence source: [MDN: Content Security Policy](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/CSP)
- Applicability: always (website)
- Expected result: A Content-Security-Policy header
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.csp`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.csp

Why: Content-Security-Policy prevents XSS and injection attacks. For AI agents that interact with your site, CSP ensures the page content hasn't been tampered with by malicious scripts.

References:

- [MDN: Content Security Policy](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/CSP) (guide)
- [OWASP CSP Cheat Sheet](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Content_Security_Policy_Cheat_Sheet.html) (guide)

Steps:

1. Start with a report-only policy and collect the violations.
2. Send the enforced policy when the violations are fixed.

   ```nginx
   add_header Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'" always;
   ```

Verify:

```bash
curl -sI https://{domain}/
```

### 5.5 X-Content-Type-Options

- Stable ID: `ia.x-content-type-options`
- Stage: Read
- Strength: MUST
- AR practices: none (mapping: none)
- Evidence type: `recommendation`
- Fix: Send X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.x-content-type-options)
- Evidence source: [MDN: X-Content-Type-Options](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/X-Content-Type-Options)
- Applicability: always (website)
- Expected result: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.x-content-type-options`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.x-content-type-options

Why: This header prevents MIME type sniffing attacks. It ensures browsers and HTTP clients interpret your content exactly as intended, reducing the risk of content injection.

References:

- [MDN: X-Content-Type-Options](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/X-Content-Type-Options) (guide)

Steps:

1. Add the header to all responses.

   ```nginx
   add_header X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff" always;
   ```

Verify:

```bash
curl -sI https://{domain}/
```

<a id="ia.frame-protection"></a>

### 5.6 X-Frame-Options / frame-ancestors

- Stable ID: `ia.frame-protection`
- Stage: Read
- Strength: MUST
- AR practices: none (mapping: none)
- Evidence type: `recommendation`
- Fix: Send X-Frame-Options or a CSP frame-ancestors directive.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.frame-protection)
- Evidence source: [MDN: X-Frame-Options](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/X-Frame-Options)
- Applicability: always (website)
- Expected result: X-Frame-Options or a Content-Security-Policy with frame-ancestors
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.frame-protection`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.frame-protection

Why: Frame protection prevents your site from being embedded in malicious iframes (clickjacking). This protects users who interact with your site through AI-suggested links.

References:

- [MDN: X-Frame-Options](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/X-Frame-Options) (guide)
- [MDN: Content Security Policy](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/CSP) (guide)

Steps:

1. Add frame-ancestors to the Content-Security-Policy, or send X-Frame-Options.

   ```nginx
   add_header Content-Security-Policy "frame-ancestors 'self'" always;
   ```

Verify:

```bash
curl -sI https://{domain}/
```

<a id="ia.cors"></a>

### 5.7 CORS

- Stable ID: `ia.cors`
- Stage: Act
- Strength: MAY
- AR practices: none (mapping: none)
- Evidence type: `recommendation`
- Fix: Send a deliberate Access-Control-Allow-Origin on API responses and never combine * with credentials.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.cors)
- Evidence source: [MDN: CORS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Guides/CORS)
- Applicability: detected_surface (api)
- Expected result: No Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * together with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.cors`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.cors

Why: CORS controls which origins can call your site from a browser. Public APIs need a deliberate CORS policy. A wildcard with credentials is not safe.

References:

- [MDN: CORS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Guides/CORS) (guide)

Steps:

1. Allow only the origins that need browser access to the API.

   ```nginx
   add_header Access-Control-Allow-Origin "https://app.example.com" always;
   ```
2. Do not send Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true with a * origin.

Verify:

```bash
curl -sI -H 'Origin: https://example.org' https://{domain}/
```

<a id="ia.tool-definition-security"></a>

### 5.10 Tool definition security

- Stable ID: `ia.tool-definition-security`
- Stage: Act
- Strength: MAY
- AR practices: none (mapping: none)
- Evidence type: `recommendation`
- Fix: Add trust annotations to WebMCP tools and keep secrets out of tool definitions.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.tool-definition-security)
- Evidence source: [WebMCP W3C Proposal](https://webmachinelearning.github.io/webmcp/)
- Applicability: detected_surface (auth)
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.tool-definition-security`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.tool-definition-security

Why: Tool definitions are visible to AI agents and may be cached or logged. Explicit trust metadata, bounded origin exposure, and lifecycle cancellation help agents invoke tools safely.

References:

- [WebMCP W3C Proposal](https://webmachinelearning.github.io/webmcp/) (guide)
- [OWASP Sensitive Data Exposure](https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/) (guide)

Steps:

1. Add readOnlyHint and untrustedContentHint annotations to each tool.

   ```javascript
   annotations: { readOnlyHint: true, untrustedContentHint: true }
   ```
2. Remove tokens, internal URLs and personal data from tool names and descriptions.
3. Pass an AbortSignal so that the page can unregister tools.

Verify:

No read-only shell check exists. Use the rescan command.

<a id="ia.auto-submit-risk"></a>

### 5.11 Auto-submit risk

- Stable ID: `ia.auto-submit-risk`
- Stage: Act
- Strength: MAY
- AR practices: none (mapping: none)
- Evidence type: `recommendation`
- Fix: Remove toolautosubmit from forms with sensitive data.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.auto-submit-risk)
- Evidence source: [WebMCP W3C Proposal](https://webmachinelearning.github.io/webmcp/)
- Applicability: detected_surface (auth)
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.auto-submit-risk`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.auto-submit-risk

Why: The toolautosubmit attribute allows AI agents to submit forms without user confirmation. This is safe for search/filter forms but risky for payment, account deletion, or password forms.

References:

- [WebMCP W3C Proposal](https://webmachinelearning.github.io/webmcp/) (guide)

Steps:

1. Find forms with toolautosubmit and a password, payment or delete action.
2. Remove toolautosubmit from these forms so that the user confirms each submit.

Verify:

No read-only shell check exists. Use the rescan command.

<a id="ia.oauth-discovery"></a>

### 5.12 OAuth discovery

- Stable ID: `ia.oauth-discovery`
- Stage: Act
- Strength: SHOULD
- AR practices: AR-ACT-01 (mapping: full)
- Evidence type: `scanner_data`
- Fix: Publish OAuth authorization server metadata at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.oauth-discovery)
- Evidence source: [agentready.org AR-ACT-01](https://www.agentready.org/#act)
- Applicability: detected_surface (auth)
- Expected result: exit code 0
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.oauth-discovery`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.oauth-discovery

Why: OAuth and OIDC discovery (RFC 8414, OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0) let agents authenticate with your APIs without manual setup.

References:

- [RFC 8414: OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server Metadata](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8414) (spec)
- [OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-discovery-1_0.html) (spec)

Steps:

1. Serve the RFC 8414 metadata with issuer, authorization_endpoint and token_endpoint.

   ```json
   {
     "issuer": "https://example.com",
     "authorization_endpoint": "https://example.com/oauth/authorize",
     "token_endpoint": "https://example.com/oauth/token",
     "code_challenge_methods_supported": ["S256"]
   }
   ```

Verify:

```bash
curl -sf https://{domain}/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server | jq -e '.issuer and .token_endpoint'
```

<a id="ia.oauth-protected-resource"></a>

### 5.13 OAuth protected resource

- Stable ID: `ia.oauth-protected-resource`
- Stage: Act
- Strength: SHOULD
- AR practices: AR-ACT-01 (mapping: full)
- Evidence type: `scanner_data`
- Fix: Publish /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource with the resource and its authorization servers.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.oauth-protected-resource)
- Evidence source: [agentready.org AR-ACT-01](https://www.agentready.org/#act)
- Applicability: detected_surface (auth)
- Expected result: exit code 0
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.oauth-protected-resource`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.oauth-protected-resource

Why: OAuth Protected Resource Metadata (RFC 9728) tells agents which authorization servers issue tokens for your APIs.

References:

- [RFC 9728: OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource Metadata](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9728) (spec)

Steps:

1. Serve the RFC 9728 metadata.

   ```json
   {
     "resource": "https://api.example.com",
     "authorization_servers": ["https://example.com"],
     "bearer_methods_supported": ["header"]
   }
   ```
2. Return WWW-Authenticate with resource_metadata on 401 responses.

Verify:

```bash
curl -sf https://{domain}/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource | jq -e '.resource and .authorization_servers'
```

<a id="ia.agent-auth-readiness"></a>

### 5.14 Agent auth readiness

- Stable ID: `ia.agent-auth-readiness`
- Stage: Act
- Strength: SHOULD
- AR practices: AR-ACT-01 (mapping: full)
- Evidence type: `scanner_data`
- Fix: Support PKCE S256, publish scopes and explain the auth flow in /auth.md.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.agent-auth-readiness)
- Evidence source: [agentready.org AR-ACT-01](https://www.agentready.org/#act)
- Applicability: detected_surface (auth)
- Expected result: exit code 0
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.agent-auth-readiness`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.agent-auth-readiness

Why: Agents need more than a login page. They need discoverable auth metadata, scoped permissions, PKCE support, and a concise walkthrough that explains how to obtain and use credentials safely.

References:

- [RFC 8414: OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server Metadata](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8414) (spec)
- [RFC 9728: OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource Metadata](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9728) (spec)
- [RFC 7636: PKCE](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7636) (spec)

Steps:

1. Add S256 to code_challenge_methods_supported in the OAuth metadata.
2. List the scopes in scopes_supported.
3. Explain the flow for agents in /auth.md.

   ```markdown
   # Authentication for agents

   Use OAuth 2.0 authorization code with PKCE S256. Request the narrowest scope for the task.
   ```

Verify:

```bash
curl -sf https://{domain}/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server | jq -e '.code_challenge_methods_supported | index("S256")'
```
